A hollow insulated cylinder of height \(2H\) and volume \(2V\) is closed from below by an insulating piston. An insulating diaphragm of mass \(m\) divides it into two initially identical chambers. The diaphragm rests on a circular ledge with a gasket providing tight contact. Both chambers initially contain gaseous helium at pressure \(p\) and temperature \(T\). A force moves the piston slowly upwards.

a
Find the lower-chamber volume \(V_0\) when gas starts leaking between the chambers.
b
Find the upper-chamber temperature \(T_1\) when the piston touches the diaphragm.
c
Find the lower-chamber temperature \(T_2\) immediately before the piston touches the diaphragm.

solution.text:
T1: A leak
a. Onset of leakage
Write \(p_u,T_u\) for upper-chamber variables and \(p_l,V_l,T_l\) for the lower ones. The upper volume remains \(V\). A fixed parcel of monatomic helium below the diaphragm is compressed adiabatically. With parcel volume \(v\),
\[0=p_l\,dv+d\left(\frac32p_lv\right)=\frac52p_l\,dv+\frac32v\,dp_l,\quad v^5p_l^3=\mathrm{const},\quad T_l^5p_l^{-2}=\mathrm{const}.\]
The diaphragm lifts enough to leak when the pressure difference balances its weight over area \(V/H\). Define
\[\Delta p=\frac{mgH}{V}=px,\qquad x=\frac{mgH}{pV},\qquad V_0=V(1+x)^{-3/5}.\]
b. Upper-chamber final temperature
During leakage \(p_l-p_u=\Delta p\) remains constant. Total gas energy conservation, including external piston work, is
\[0=p_l\,dV_l+\frac32d(p_uV+p_lV_l)=\frac52p_l\,d(V+V_l)+\frac32(V+V_l)\,dp_l.\]
\[(V+V_l)^5p_l^3=\mathrm{const}.\]
At leakage onset \(V_l=V_0\) and \(p_l=p(1+x)\). At piston contact \(V_l\to0\). Thus
\[p_l'=p\left[1+(1+x)^{3/5}\right]^{5/3},\qquad p_u'=p_l'-px.\]
All the gas, twice the initial mole number of either chamber, ends in the upper volume \(V\). Its equation of state gives
\[T_1=\frac T2\left(\left[1+(1+x)^{3/5}\right]^{5/3}-x\right).\]
c. Lower-chamber limiting temperature
Apply the parcel invariant \(T_l^5p_l^{-2}=T^5p^{-2}\) to the remaining lower gas as its amount tends to zero:
\[T_2=T\left(\frac{p_l'}p\right)^{2/5}=T\left[1+(1+x)^{3/5}\right]^{2/3}.\]
